stories.headline: OpenAI Proposes Robot Taxes, Public Wealth Fund in 'Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age'

key_facts.fact: OpenAI published a 13-page policy document titled 'Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age: Ideas to Keep People First' on April 6, presented as a starting point for debate.
key_facts.excerpt: 13-page policy document titled 'Industrial Policy for the Intelligence Age'... Presented as starting point for debate, not fixed prescription

key_facts.fact: The plan proposes a nationally managed public wealth fund seeded by AI companies, modeled after Alaska's Permanent Fund oil dividend, to give every American a stake in AI-driven growth.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI proposes seeding a national fund with contributions from AI companies. The fund would invest in AI firms and businesses adopting the technology, then distribute returns directly to American citizens—modeled after Alaska's Permanent Fund oil dividend structure.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI proposes taxing businesses that replace human workers with automated systems to compensate for reduced payroll tax revenue funding Social Security, Medicaid, and food assistance.
key_facts.excerpt: Tax businesses that replace human workers with automated systems to compensate for reduced payroll tax revenue that funds Social Security, Medicaid, and food assistance.

key_facts.fact: The document proposes auto-triggering safety nets: benefits like unemployment payments and wage insurance increase automatically when AI-driven job displacement hits preset thresholds, then phase out when conditions improve.
key_facts.excerpt: Benefits like unemployment payments and wage insurance would increase automatically when AI-driven job displacement hits preset thresholds, then phase out when conditions improve.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI proposes pilot programs testing 32-hour workweeks at full pay, framed as an 'efficiency dividend' from AI productivity gains.
key_facts.excerpt: Pilot programs testing 32-hour workweeks at full pay, framed as 'efficiency dividend'

key_facts.fact: Altman warns cyberattacks are 'totally possible' within one year and bioweapon creation is 'no longer theoretical,' describing them as the most immediate AI threats.
key_facts.excerpt: He stated cyberattacks and bioweapons represent the 'most immediate' AI threats, describing cyberattacks as 'totally possible' within one year and bioweapon creation as 'no longer theoretical.'

key_facts.fact: Altman told Axios that AI superintelligence is so close and disruptive that America needs a new social contract on the scale of the Progressive Era and the New Deal during the Great Depression.
key_facts.excerpt: Altman told Axios he feels such urgency about the power of coming AI models that OpenAI is unveiling a New Deal for superintelligence... He says AI will soon be so mindbending that America needs a new social contract

stories.headline: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar Excluded From Key Meetings as IPO Timeline Clash With Altman Widens

key_facts.fact: Sam Altman excluded CFO Sarah Friar from a major investor meeting regarding server procurement and other key financial discussions.
key_facts.excerpt: Friar was excluded from a major investor meeting regarding server procurement... excluded from certain financial discussions

key_facts.fact: Friar began reporting to Fidji Simo, former Instacart CEO who oversees OpenAI's applications business, instead of directly to CEO Altman — a departure from typical CFO reporting lines.
key_facts.excerpt: Friar now reports to Fidji Simo, the former Instacart CEO who now oversees OpenAI's applications business—a shift suggesting reduced direct access to Altman.

key_facts.fact: Altman has committed OpenAI to spend $600 billion over five years on computing infrastructure and privately said he wants to go public as soon as Q4 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: CEO Sam Altman wants the IPO as soon as Q4, despite the company spending over $200 billion before generating cash.

key_facts.fact: Friar has privately said OpenAI may not be ready for a 2026 IPO, citing procedural readiness, compliance maturity, and financial risks from aggressive spending.
key_facts.excerpt: Friar's concern: Company may lack procedural readiness and compliance maturity for this timeline... Financial risks tied to aggressive spending commitments

key_facts.fact: OpenAI anticipates spending $121 billion on computing power for AI research in 2028, with expected losses of $85 billion that year even after nearly doubling sales.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI anticipates spending $121 billion on computing power for AI research in 2028, with expected losses of $85 billion that year even after nearly doubling sales.

key_facts.fact: Both executives released a joint statement claiming alignment on compute strategy, stating they have 'both been directly involved in every consequential compute decision.'
key_facts.excerpt: Both executives released a unified statement emphasizing alignment on compute strategy, stating they've 'both been directly involved in every consequential compute decision.'

stories.headline: WSJ: OpenAI and Anthropic Inference Costs Exceed Half of Revenue, Profitability Paths Diverge

key_facts.fact: Both OpenAI and Anthropic have projected profitability to investors with and without training costs, with inference costs exceeding half of total revenue for both companies.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI and Anthropic have projected profitability to investors with and without training costs, and report inference costs exceeding half of revenue

key_facts.fact: Anthropic experienced inference costs 23% higher than internally anticipated, pushing gross margins to approximately 40%. OpenAI's projected gross margin is 46% in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic experienced 23% higher inference costs than anticipated... OpenAI projected gross margin: 46% in 2025 (including non-paying users). Anthropic projected gross margin: 40% in 2025

key_facts.fact: Anthropic annualized revenue reached $19 billion by early 2026, closing the gap with OpenAI's $25 billion — a difference of just $6 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic: Annualized revenue: $19 billion... OpenAI: Annualized revenue: $25 billion

key_facts.fact: Anthropic projects cash flow positive by 2028, while OpenAI targets 2030 — a 3-4 year divergence. OpenAI projects $21.2 billion in cash burn for 2029.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic: Cash flow positive by 2028. OpenAI: Cash flow positive by 2030... OpenAI projected 2029 cash burn: $21.2 billion

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has a $21 billion Google TPU purchase commitment, while OpenAI has 'taped out' a proprietary inference chip to reduce reliance on third-party hardware.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic: $21 billion Google TPU purchase commitment. OpenAI: Developing proprietary inference chip ('taped out')

key_facts.fact: Anthropic derives 86% of revenue from API sales with ~9 customers spending $100M+ annually, while OpenAI gets 40% from business customers (~$5.2 billion).
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic: 86% from API sales; remainder from Claude subscriptions. ~9 customers spending $100M+ annually. OpenAI: 40% from business customers (~$5.2 billion)

stories.headline: Tufts Neuro-Symbolic AI Achieves 95% Accuracy With 100x Less Energy Than Standard Models

key_facts.fact: Researchers at Tufts University led by Matthias Scheutz developed a neuro-symbolic visual-language-action (VLA) system that combines neural networks with symbolic reasoning, achieving up to 100x energy reduction.
key_facts.excerpt: Researchers have unveiled a radically more efficient approach that could slash AI energy use by up to 100x while actually improving accuracy... led by Matthias Scheutz, Karol Family Applied Technology Professor

key_facts.fact: The neuro-symbolic VLA achieved a 95% success rate on the Tower of Hanoi puzzle, compared with just 34% for standard systems, and 78% on unfamiliar complex variants where traditional models scored 0%.
key_facts.excerpt: Neuro-symbolic VLA achieved 95% success rate vs. 34% for standard systems on Tower of Hanoi puzzle. Achieved 78% success on unfamiliar complex puzzle variants (traditional models: 0%)

key_facts.fact: Training required only 1% of the energy of standard VLA systems (34 minutes vs. 36+ hours), and operational energy consumption was just 5% of conventional approaches.
key_facts.excerpt: Training requires only 1% of energy used by standard VLA systems. Operational energy consumption: 5% of conventional approaches. Training time: 34 minutes vs. 36+ hours for conventional approaches

key_facts.fact: The approach focuses on robotics VLA models that extend LLM capabilities by incorporating vision and physical movement, unlike chatbot-style LLMs like ChatGPT.
key_facts.excerpt: Unlike familiar large language models such as ChatGPT and Gemini, the team focuses on AI systems used in robotics known as visual-language-action (VLA) models, which extend LLM capabilities by incorporating vision and physical movement.

key_facts.fact: The work will be presented at the International Conference of Robotics and Automation (ICRA) in Vienna in May 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The work will be presented at the International Conference of Robotics and Automation in Vienna in May

stories.headline: Japan Targets 30% Global Physical AI Market by 2040, Budgets $2.5B for AI and Robotics

key_facts.fact: Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) announced it aims to capture 30% of the global physical AI market by 2040, building on Japan's existing 70% share of global industrial robotics.
key_facts.excerpt: Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry announced in March 2026 that it aims to build a domestic physical AI sector and capture a 30% share of the global market by 2040.

key_facts.fact: Tokyo budgeted 387.3 billion yen specifically for domestic AI foundation models, data infrastructure, and physical AI, within a broader 1.23 trillion yen package for AI and semiconductor development in fiscal year 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Tokyo budgeted ¥387.3 billion specifically for the development of domestic AI foundation models, data infrastructure, and physical AI, within a broader ¥1.23 trillion package earmarked for AI and semiconductor development in fiscal year 2026.

key_facts.fact: Japan projects a shortage of 570,000 care workers by 2040, with nursing positions drawing only 1 applicant per 4.25 openings, driving the urgency of physical AI adoption.
key_facts.excerpt: Japan projects a shortage of 570,000 care workers by 2040, with nursing positions drawing only one applicant for every 4.25 openings.

key_facts.fact: FANUC announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to advance physical AI, enabling robots to interpret voice commands and automatically generate Python code without specialized programming skills.
key_facts.excerpt: FANUC announced a collaboration with NVIDIA to advance physical AI, enabling robots to interpret voice commands and automatically generate Python code, allowing operators to give verbal instructions without specialized programming skills.

key_facts.fact: Japan's population declined for a 14th straight year, with working-age adults at just 59.6% of the total, a share projected to shrink by nearly 15 million over the next 20 years.

stories.headline: Medvi Controversy Exposes AI-Powered Healthcare Fraud: Fake Doctors, Deepfakes, FDA Warning

key_facts.fact: The New York Times profiled Medvi on April 2 as a two-employee company projecting $1.8 billion in 2026 revenue, presenting it as proof of Sam Altman's prediction that AI could enable billion-dollar one-person companies.
key_facts.excerpt: The New York Times initially featured Medvi as 'a shining example of AI-powered efficiency'... generated $1.8 billion in revenue... with just two employees

key_facts.fact: Gary Marcus published a viral rebuttal on April 5, calling Medvi 'a cautionary tale' about AI misuse rather than a success story, triggering widespread criticism of the NYT profile.
key_facts.excerpt: Gary Marcus later cited the case as 'a cautionary tale'... appalled by the puff piece NYT wrote about 'billion dollar' company Medvi

key_facts.fact: The FDA sent Medvi warning letter #721455 on February 20, 2026, for misbranding violations including falsely implying the company compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide and suggesting FDA approval of compounded products.
key_facts.excerpt: On February 20, 2026, the FDA sent MEDVi warning letter #721455 identifying misbranding violations... falsely suggested the company compounded the semaglutide and tirzepatide it sold.

key_facts.fact: Founder Matthew Gallagher created 800+ Facebook pages posing as individual doctors with fabricated medical titles, with over 5,000 active Medvi-related ads running on Meta's platform.
key_facts.excerpt: Gallagher created 800+ Facebook pages posing as individual doctors... more than 5,000 active MEDVi-related ads on Meta's platform, including some running under apparent fictitious personas with fabricated medical titles

key_facts.fact: Medvi used AI-generated deepfake before-and-after photos in its marketing, and a January 2026 data breach exposed records of approximately 1.6 million patients.
key_facts.excerpt: used AI to create ethically questionable advertising, fake doctor profiles on social media, fabricated videos, and generated before-and-after comparisons... a threat actor breached systems and claimed to have exfiltrated records from approximately 1.6 million patients
